title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Graph State Generation in Photonic Quantum Computers
problem: In photonic quantum computers (PQCs), generating graph states (entangled photon collections) requires finding an optimal generation sequence over quantum emitters, where three fidelity-critical metrics — generation time, number of emitters used, and number of CZ gates — are jointly minimized. Existing compilation frameworks either face exponential search complexity or fail to guarantee optimal results due to their non-deterministic properties.
motivation: Graph state generation quality directly determines photonic quantum computation fidelity; suboptimal generation sequences waste scarce quantum emitter resources and increase CZ gate count, both of which degrade output fidelity in near-term PQC hardware.
method: RLGS uses reinforcement learning (an AI approach where an algorithm learns through trial and error) to optimize how graph states (entangled collections of photons) are generated in photonic quantum computers. It creates a structured "map" of the quantum circuit that organizes two-qubit gates (operations on pairs of quantum bits) and their dependencies (which operations must happen first), allowing the RL agent to search for generation sequences that reduce generation time, emitter count, and CZ gate insertions simultaneously. The system balances competing constraints: minimizing the sequential depth of gates while also reducing crosstalk (unwanted interference between qubits).
key_novelty: RLGS restructures the quantum circuit into a "map" that the RL agent can navigate, converting what would otherwise be an exponentially difficult search over gate dependencies into a tractable optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes generation time, emitter count, and CZ gate insertions.
contributions: A map-based framework that abstracts quantum circuit dependencies for efficient qubit reuse and generation sequence optimization.
An RL-guided search strategy that jointly minimizes generation time, emitter count, and CZ gate count for photonic quantum computers.
Average generation time reductions of 31.1%, 49.6%, and 57.5% for small, medium, and large graph states vs. state-of-the-art.
Emitter count reductions of 13.9-17.5% and CZ gate reductions of 37.7-57.8% across benchmark graph states.

metrics.speedup: 31.1-57.5% reduction in generation time vs. state-of-the-art (small to large graph states)

limitations: Not discussed; scalability of the RL training to very large graph states and convergence time are not addressed.
primary_theme: RL-guided compilation for photonic quantum graph state generation
